newsitem.title: USA: Florida lawmakers vote to ban LaRoche sleep drug.
newsitem.headline: Florida lawmakers vote to ban LaRoche sleep drug.

text.p: Florida lawmakers voted unanimously on Thursday to outlaw the drug Rohypnol, saying the so-called "date rape" drug had no therapeutic use and was becoming the drug of choice of sexual predators.
The drug has come under fire from law enforcement officials who say sex crime victims unwittingly ingest it, often becoming incapacitated and losing their memories of the event.
"This is the single most significant protection for women that we'll pass this year," said Rep. Ken Pruitt., R-Port St. Lucie, and a principal sponsor of the bill.

The bill outlawing the drug sailed through the Florida House 118-0 on Thursday morning, and was passed 33-0 in the Senate in the afternoon. Florida Governor Lawton Chiles was expected to sign it into law.
The bill changes the drug's classification from a Schedule IV to Schedule I drug, a group that includes marijuana, cocaine and LSD.
Three other states, Idaho, Minnesota and Oklahoma, have outlawed the drug.

Manufactured by Hoffman-LaRoche Inc., the drug is widely used in Europe and Latin America for sleep disorders. About 10 times more potent than Valium, it is believed to be smuggled into the United States from Mexico and Colombia.
Hoffman-LaRoche is a U.S. affiliate of Swiss pharmaceutical group Roche Holding Ltd..
Last year, U.S. lawmakers stiffened penalties for misuse of the drug, but retained its legal status.
Opponents say the drug is being used by sexual predators to incapacitate their victims, who often have no recollection of the incident.
"Imagine the terror of waking up in the morning knowing something has been done to you but you don't know what," Senate sponsor Don Sullivan, R-Seminole, said.
